pr_title: Add support for playing storyboards beyond gameplay end time
pr_body:
Closes [#11982](https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/11982)

![storyboardtesting1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40254686/114913770-9788c680-9def-11eb-83fe-aea2ee9ba7c1.gif)

### **Description** ###
Allows a user to skip a storyboard outro if there is one after the playable portion of the beatmap. 
Previously, the score was instantly shown after the last hit object regardless of the storyboard. Now, a skip overlay is shown and offers the option to skip to the end to display the score. This is disabled in multiplayer like skipping the intro.

- Adds a new `IStoryboardElementWithDuration` implemented by `IStoryboardSprite` and added an extension method `GetEndTime` to `IStoryboardElement` to calculate the end time of the storyboard.
- Skipping the outro, holding esc and waiting until the outro ends leads to `updateCompletionState` to avoid bypassing conditions checked before completion. 

### **Tests** ###
- Visual tests in `TestSceneStoryboardWithOutro`*
  - Skip outro with space
  - Skip outro with esc
  - Without skipping outro
  - Storyboard ends before score completion
  - Storyboard ends during fail animation
  - While toggling storyboard during the map
- ~~[ ] With cinema mod~~
  
*Unit tests can sometimes fail due to a bug described in #12426

### **Behavior Compared to Stable** ###

| Case                    | Original (stable)                                 | New behavior                                 |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Player pressed skip     | Show score instantly                              | Show score instantly                         |
| Player exited using Esc | Show score instantly                              | Show score instantly                         |
| End of outro reached    | (unsure if with or without delay) shows the score | Show the score after `RESULTS_DISPLAY_DELAY` |

Co-Authored-By: @marlinabowring
pr_comments: I updated the branch so it includes `TestSceneEditorSelection`.
Should the skip overlay be shown during the outro if Cinema mod is enabled? I noticed that on stable the skip overlay is not shown at all.
Probably not, but that would be a separate issue / PR (along with hiding it during the intro).

> As a good step, scheduleCompletion should never be called from anywhere else except for updateCompletionState.

I think it's fine for the skip outro overlay to call `scheduleCompletion` right? Because the overlay is shown after  `prepareScoreForDisplay` is non-null.
I don't think so, it would still bypass certain conditions in `updateCompletionState`. Any reason not to call it there?

> I don't think so, it would still bypass certain conditions in `updateCompletionState`. Any reason not to call it there?

If the skip overlay calls `updateCompletionState`, then the score is shown after a delay (`RESULTS_DISPLAY_DELAY=1000`), which doesn't match stable where it seems to be shown instantly.

~~A solution I thought of was to add a new parameter `showInstantly` to `updateCompletionState` that's false by default, and true if called by the skip overlay.~~ actually that didn't work nvm
If that's how you'll use it then the parameter should be renamed to something like `skipGameplayOutro` (also should definitely add a `return;` there)

I wonder, what conditions could be bypassed if the skip overlay called `scheduleCompletion()` directly? Aren't all the conditions (`HasFailed`, `ShowResults`) already checked in `updateCompletionState` before the skip overlay is shown?

Still doesn't change my mind, `updateCompletionState` should be the only method responsible for calling `scheduleCompletion`, regardless of whether the order of things show that the outro skip overlay can bypass checks just fine.
Alright, I also made `PerformExit()` call `updateCompletionState` the same way the skip overlay does for when the player holds esc during the outro.
I've made some changes to get this into a state I'm happy with merging. Would appreciate one more review though.

review_comments: While I think this is fine for now for simplicity, there may be a point in the future where this needs to be refactored into a single overlay able to handle multiple skip operations (for instance, when implementing #12493).

Yeah, not to mention that the current way would break when rewinding before the storyboard outro part, which can be fixed easily with a single skip overlay (potentially by using the existing `PeriodTracker` to tell whether a period can be skipped).
Rather than a reply to an inline comment, that seems like something you should post in a review? It is an oversight that blocks this from being usable.

Right, I thought it's not easily solvable and something to resolve in a follow-up PR or something, but now that I think about it, it can be solved and does currently block it from being usable, will do.
You included this note but didn't follow it yourself 😅

To reiterate on https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/12432#discussion_r615210904, this is how I thought about having it https://github.com/frenzibyte/osu/commit/016509a520f1aecbd4f1d9d64484c39bddcd1a4e, while the current solution pushed here is simpler, the changes I made in the linked commit keeps `DimmableStoryboard` from having to expose things in `DrawableStoryboard` and initialize with a sane default.

I'm fine either way, but going to leave this as a comment.

@frenzibyte your version is a bit weird (private event for some reason with a separate binding method, instead of just having the event public and then invoking it at the right time), and I honestly prefer the variant as written here. Makes sense to me to have `HasStoryboardEnded` on both `DrawableStoryboard` and this.
